items.reason: Already closed before this cycle: I read every run: block in agent-dispatch.yml and autofix.yml and neither interpolates any expression into a shell — issue title/body/comment, PR head ref and PR number all arrive via env: and are read as quoted variables — and scripts/security/check-actions.mjs enforces that as a blocking run-injection rule via npm run security:actions in ci.yml, with fixtures in scripts/review/__tests__/gate-check.test.mjs including one that walks every workflow in the tree (line 343) and one hostile-issue-title case (line 307).

Three of the four missing bullets are already closed: .github/workflows/review.yml has an agent-review job that hands the diff to Claude, scripts/review/rubric.mjs assembles the rubric from .claude/CLAUDE.md and docs/architecture/decisions/ (no second copy to drift), the review posts as a PR comment and exits 1 on a blocking finding, and .github/rulesets/main.json lists 'Agent review (judgement)' as a required status check with review:gate --verify asking GitHub whether the ruleset is really applied. I closed the fourth (no documented recovery path for a dispatch that stops) rather than leaving it, but that alone does not close the item as stated.

Conventional commits are already enforced, not merely habitual — .githooks/commit-msg runs scripts/release/commit-msg.mjs locally (wired by the prepare installer, verified by npm run hooks:check) and the 'Commit convention (subjects the changelog is cut from)' job in ci.yml is a required status check in .github/rulesets/main.json, with fixtures in npm run test:release. The two genuinely open pieces need capabilities this session lacks: adding Prettier/Biome needs network to regenerate package-lock.json (a devDependency added without it makes npm ci fail hard), and dropping F821 from ruff.toml needs ruff on the machine to prove the tree is clean — inventing either answer would turn CI red rather than raise the bar. Note that a repo-wide formatter is also a recorded position here (autofix.yml and change-review.md both state this tree is deliberately not formatter-owned), so adoption is a maintainer decision, not a gap to fill silently.

lessons: Read the repo before believing the scan: in xkazm04/kp all three dispatched items named machinery that already existed and operated (review.yml with a repo-owned rubric and a required-check ruleset, a run-injection ratchet with whole-tree fixtures, a commit-msg hook plus a required CI job). Prior Ascent cycles had shipped them; the scan's snapshot predated the commits. Verifying first turned three would-be duplicate implementations into one real fix.

This repository's own idiom is that a guard must be provably wired, not merely present: every checker under scripts/ has dependency-free node:test fixtures, a CI job, and an entry in .github/rulesets/main.json, and gate-check.mjs exists solely to catch a required check whose name no job reports. Match that shape when adding anything here — an unfixtured guard reads as decoration to both the maintainer and the next scan.

GitHub Actions job-level `timeout-minutes` cancels the run, and a cancelled run skips `if: failure()` steps — so any 'report what went wrong' step needs a smaller step-level budget on whatever can hang, or it stays silent on exactly the outcome it was written for.
